id_and_class.summary: Physicist Paul Davies speculates that information may be more fundamental than matter or energy and that consciousness is tied to this informational substrate, perhaps as a causal agent in a ‘middle layer’ between physical law and the complexity of life. He also leans toward Wheeler’s view that conscious observers take part in shaping the universe’s history.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness Rooted in a Hidden Informational Layer

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is linked to deep informational structures, and Davies suggests it ‘may be a deep informational principle that lies at the root of physical law itself’.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Mind and matter both rest on information, which Davies treats as possibly more basic than particles or forces. He does not commit to a precise mind–body relation.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Unclear (Davies allows that consciousness may emerge from informational structures or may be a principle underlying physical law)
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Information as a fundamental, causally effective feature of reality; physical law; possibly law-like teleological constraints.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Davies stresses that all science starts in consciousness: our observations, stitched together, are the starting point of inquiry.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: A hypothesized ‘middle layer’ of reality between physical law and the observed complexity of life, where information acts as a new kind of cause.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Consciousness in general and its place in cosmology; life and mind as informational phenomena
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Informational causation: information has causal power, not only descriptive value, and may operate in a layer between fundamental physics and biology.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: In complex informational systems such as brains, and possibly in the informational structure of the universe as a whole.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Consciousness may act as a causal force, and Davies suggests that the existence of conscious observers may have affected or selected the quantum histories of the universe.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Reality itself may be an informational construct, in the spirit of Wheeler’s ‘it from bit’.
mechanism_and_dynamics.evolutionary_account: Davies speculates that the laws of physics might somehow ‘know’ to bring about life and consciousness, through teleological or information-constrained law-like behavior.
core_claims_and_evidence: Information may be more fundamental than matter or energy.
Current physical theories may be incomplete until they include information and consciousness in a new way.
A missing layer of reality between physical law and life may involve information as a causal agent, and consciousness may reside there.
Conscious observation may be integral to the universe’s existence and history, as in Wheeler’s participatory anthropic principle.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Theoretical and philosophical speculation grounded in physics and cosmology

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Davies does not offer a complete theory of consciousness, so the proposal has no specified mechanism to test. The suggestion that physical laws ‘know’ to produce life and mind invokes teleology that most physicists reject.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: What informational causation consists of, and how consciousness relates to it, are left open.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Coherent with information-first views in physics such as Wheeler’s, but the status of consciousness (emergent or foundational) remains undecided.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Davies holds that consciousness plays a fundamental role in the evolution of the universe and that physical law may be directed toward producing it.
